history.summary: The Military Mahadev Temple on Congress Road (NH-4A) in the Camp area of Belagavi Cantonment, Karnataka, is a Lord Shiva temple built for and by the Indian Army — hence its name. The foundation stone was laid on 18 January 1954 and the temple was opened to the public on 24 January 1955 by Lieutenant General S.M. Shrinagesh; it was raised for the worship of personnel of the Maratha Light Infantry Regimental Centre and remains maintained by the Army. The central shrine houses a striking black Shivling described as guarded by a multi-hooded serpent — sources disagree on five versus seven hoods (CONFLICT — verify). The complex combines a temple with landscaped gardens, a children's park, a mini zoo (deer, emus, rabbits, tortoises), a statue of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and fort models, making it a popular family outing as well as a place of worship.

name: Military Mahadev Temple
town_description: Belagavi (formerly Belgaum) is a historic city in north-western Karnataka on the foothills of the Western Ghats, near the borders with Maharashtra and Goa. Its fort, dating to the 12th-century Ratta dynasty, and its blend of Kannada, Marathi and Goan cultures make it a major commercial and educational centre. The city is noted for its Shiva temples, including the ancient Kapileshwar Temple and the Army-maintained Military Mahadev Temple.

travel.road: Congress Road (NH-4A), Camp area, at the start of the Cantonment; easily accessible by bus, auto-rickshaw or taxi

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Mahashivaratri and Mondays draw the largest crowds
